# compute_neighbor_diversity { #dyf.compute_neighbor_diversity }

```python
compute_neighbor_diversity(embeddings, k=15, neighbors=None)
```

Compute neighbor diversity for each point.

Diversity measures how dissimilar a point's neighbors are to each other.
High diversity indicates a "general" concept that connects multiple topics.
Low diversity indicates a "specific" concept within a tight cluster.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type                                             | Description                                                       | Default    |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| embeddings | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`)         | Normalized embeddings (n, d)                                      | _required_ |
| k          | [int](`int`)                                     | Number of neighbors to consider                                   | `15`       |
| neighbors  | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) \| None | Pre-computed k-NN indices (n, k+1). If None, computed internally. | `None`     |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                     | Description                                                  |
|--------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [np](`numpy`).[ndarray](`numpy.ndarray`) | Diversity scores for each point (n,). Higher = more general. |

## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> diversity = compute_neighbor_diversity(embeddings, k=15)
>>> general_idx = np.argsort(diversity)[-10:]  # Most general concepts
>>> specific_idx = np.argsort(diversity)[:10]  # Most specific concepts
